svg.text: Fashion stylist: how the service is built and how a request moves through it

POST /recommend takes a sentence like "an outfit for the beach this summer under $150", plans 1 to 5 product slots with an LLM (brand and all), retrieves per slot with dense + BM25 search over 100,000 indexed listings behind a type gate, reranks each slot with an LLM, and returns k
products per slot with reasons. Solid arrows carry data, dashed arrows are LLM calls (both directions), grey boxes are files on disk, the dotted box is the only external service.
1. Offline, run once per catalog: raw json to a verified index directory
gzip from the McAuley lab mirror
json object per line: title, price,
price known for 6% of rows; categories
empty for every row, so no taxonomy
streams the file, one typed row
bad lines skipped and counted, written
to a temp file then renamed; ~30 s
sha256 of every file into meta.json
2.7 min for 100K rows on a laptop
GPU; built in a scratch dir, swapped in

Startup check (SearchIndex.load): pipeline version, embedding model name and revision, row counts, row order (row_ids vs catalog), sha256 of every file, finite embeddings. Anything off and the service refuses to start rather than serve misaligned rows.
2. Online, one request: plan, retrieve, rerank, select (one deadline, every fallback reported)
chars, k 1 to 10, finite prices, min
request id, per-ip rate limit, in-flight
regex planner if the LLM fails or there
all slot queries embedded in one
type gate for LLM plans (only title
type matches once k exist); a
Anthropic or OpenAI SDK behind one async method complete_json(system, user,
structured output parsed into pydantic models; typed errors: auth, rate limit, timeout,
global concurrency cap (LLM_CONCURRENCY = 8), per stage budgets: plan 15 s,
LLM_PROVIDER=none runs the whole service without a key: regex plan + hybrid retrieval +
round robin across slots by rank
a product group fills at most one
below k, unpriced items under a

fallback is a warning in the
candidate pools: max(10, k x slots) per slot, grouped, masked
